title: Owner runs W-001 over whole C:\ to discharge SL-089 criterion 3
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: 1. A person has run W-001 over the whole of C:\ unelevated, from pwsh as `-Root C:\`, with the wcifs-layer-store precaution on, and the run wrote .taad/slices/SL-089/c-drive-run.json (scope whole-drive, elevated false, checkerElevated false, checkerControls all true, verdict held): missing
2. In c-drive-run.json the panel's rows equal the engine's failed-folder count: rows = header = coreUnreadable: missing
3. No refused-then-listed folder is a row (oracle.openRefusedButOpenable 0, no console 'LEAK:' line), while about 306,000 such folders exist on C:\: missing
4. No row has an empty reason, and no folder is a row twice (emptyReasons 0, duplicates 0): missing

5. The whole-drive counts are near the expected values: about 682–684 rows (≈652 code 5, ≈28 code 363, ≈2 code 1920); about 30 leftover rows (oracle.leftoverRows code363 + reparse); verdict held; duplicates 0 (SC-136/SC-138 expectations folded in): missing

Criterion 5 asks for about 682-684 rows (652/28/2), but those counts were measured with the container layer store scanned. The run the slice requires leaves the store out, and Test-W001 fails a whole-drive run that does not. Does the person accept criterion 5 as met when the record's counts are explained item by item: rows at most about 660, code 363 27-28, code 1920 0-2, notScanned 1, every difference from 682 named? The only like-for-like alternative is a scan with the precaution off, which brings back the wcifs.sys pool growth.
Uncontested; one proposal. Where the criterion-5 reconciliation table lives (the new SL-107 doc, or appended to SL-089-seams.md) is a placement choice the reviewer may reverse.

Uncontested; one proposal. Teeing the console into artifacts\ versus asking the person to keep the window's scrollback is a convenience choice. The design picks Tee-Object because the hook log is deleted.
The whole-C:\ W-001 run and the record .taad/slices/SL-089/c-drive-run.json: the person's run (SC-136, SC-138); no engine stage may make it.

Cases C-009 to C-013 of the design (timeout, elevated shell, precaution off, app stopped mid-scan, -Root C: without backslash, committed file holding a path): marked not material and needing a click, an elevated session, a long run or a code change.
Exposing the refused-then-listed count in the schema-1 report: filed for later in the design.
Any edit to WindowCases.ps1, to the guard comment at lines 6199-6200, or to .taad/slices/SL-089/index.json.
An architecture-record edit: no block's sentence became untrue.
Once the person's record is committed, the awaiting_file entry in plants.json can be dropped; the harness works either way.
If the person's run ends TIMEOUT, raise the 1,200 literal in Invoke-HookedRun 'rows' inside Test-W001 (then run WindowMutants -Mutant All per Q-114).
Expose the refused-then-listed count (LastAccessAsked minus Kept minus Unreadable.Count, per U-102) in the report so a W-001 record can show the roughly 306,000 context figure.

critique missed: The design claimed the appended counts-only rule 'matches no file until the person commits it, and the gates treat that as a pass (Q-012)', and that no code changes. It never asked which repo-level consumers read Fitness's unmatched list. The repo's rules harness (eng/rules-harness/harness.py check_clean and describe_unmatched) refuses a clean baseline with an unmatched rule (exit 2), and RuleCases C-007 asserts 'none unmatched'. A check was owed: run harness.py clean baseline on a tree with the rule and no record.

critique missed: The design's capture command rested on a recalled claim that Tee-Object streams a native child's stdout. Critique M1 checked the missing artifacts\ folder but not the decoding. The parent pwsh decodes the child's output with [Console]::OutputEncoding, which is OEM 437 on this PC. A LEAK path with non-OEM characters, the capture's only purpose, came out as '?' or a lookalike, in the file and on screen. A check was owed: pipe a child that prints U+4E2D and U+0151 through the command at the default code page.

critique missed: The m3 disposition ('in the design record, set would_force_resynthesis to false') and the O-002/O-015 builder instruction ordered a hand-edit of an engine-exported design-slice-1.json. Q-106 already says those files are overwritten on refresh. The edit was reverted and the obligation was recorded discharged against a tree that disagrees.

caused_by.reason: 1 obligation(s) landed on this stage after it passed (O-016), so nothing downstream was ever going to carry them out and the merge would have refused. Sent back with what raised them: O-016 (fix): M1 (major): The rule's harness rows S83, S84, S85, S86 and P36 (eng/rules-harness/plants.json) all use op new-file at .taad/slices/SL-089/c-drive-run.json. Planting._create marks a row PLANT-BROKEN when its target already exists. copy_tree copies every tracked or untracked-not-ignored file into the scratch copy, so the record will be there once the person's run writes it. From that moment every `harness.py` run with --scenario all or plants exits 1 with 5 PLANT-BROKEN rows. Q-027 makes that run a required validate check for any slice that touches .taad/fitness.yaml, ArchitectureRulesTests.cs or eng/rules-harness, and most slices append a rule to fitness.yaml. Those later slices would fail validate on rows they did not touch. I reproduced it: with the record present in a temp tree, harness.batches plus Planting.apply set broken = '.taad/slices/SL-089/c-drive-run.json already exists, so it cannot be created' for all five rows. The builder's follow-up calls keeping awaiting_file 'harmless' and does not mention the rows. RuleCases does not catch this: its harness cases pass --only lists that leave these rows out. Change Planting._create so that a new-file row whose path is listed under awaiting_file overwrites an existing file. Before writing, record the file's bytes in self.saved and self.manifest and do not add it to self.created; restore() then writes the bytes back and checks the hash. Prove it with one run in a repo copy that holds a record at that path: `harness.py --only S83,S84,S85,S86,P36` must exit 0. A RuleCases case doing the same would pin it.
